# mcp.vin — Free VIN Decoder & MCP Server

> Comprehensive LLM-readable documentation for mcp.vin
> See also: [llms.txt](https://mcp.vin/llms.txt) (summary version)

## About

mcp.vin combines free public vehicle data from NHTSA, EPA and manufacturer sources, with representative stock photos. Public lookups require no API key or account; rate limits apply. Saved vehicles and preferences require a website account. Available as a unified website, REST API, and MCP server for AI assistants.

The current hosted and GitHub source release is 1.7.0. All 22 tools, grouped by task, are listed at https://mcp.vin/api/tools and through MCP tools/list. Research endpoint details are at https://mcp.vin/research/api.json; exact coverage is at https://mcp.vin/api/research/capabilities. The npm package may lag the hosted and source release.

The website combines VIN reports, comparison, configuration research, safety evidence, ownership costs, saved vehicles, coverage and developer tools. Old /research/ links retain their query parameters and section destinations.

VIN recall status is separate from model-year campaigns. Tesla and Ford provide open/completed states; GM includes completed or administratively closed states with repair dates only when supplied; Honda provides active recalls; Nissan provides positive open safety records; Mopar mixes open recall/campaign records. Toyota, Hyundai and Kia require interactive official verification. Unknown values are never zero. These sources are not a complete service history.

- URL: https://mcp.vin
- Source: https://github.com/keptlive/vin-mcp
- npm: vin-mcp
- Smithery: @keptlive/vin-mcp
- License: MIT

## Data Sources

| Source | Data Provided |
|--------|--------------|
| NHTSA vPIC | Make, model, year, trim, body class, engine specs, transmission, drive type, weight, plant info, 140+ decoded fields |
| NHTSA Recalls | Model-year campaigns with component, summary, consequence, and remedy; not VIN repair status |
| NHTSA Complaints | Consumer complaints with crash, fire, injury, and death statistics |
| NHTSA Safety Ratings | NCAP star ratings for overall, frontal, side, and rollover crash tests |
| EPA Fuel Economy | City/highway/combined MPG, annual fuel cost, CO2 emissions, EV range and charge time |
| IMAGIN.studio | Stock vehicle photos from multiple angles |

## REST API

Base URL: `https://mcp.vin`

### GET /api/vin/:vin — Full VIN Decode

Aggregates all 6 data sources into a single JSON response.

Parameters:
- `vin` (path, required): 17-character Vehicle Identification Number

Response fields:
- `valid` (boolean): Whether the VIN passed validation
- `vin` (string): The normalized VIN
- `validation` (object): Checksum result, WMI country/manufacturer, model year decode
- `vehicle` (object): Year, make, model, trim, body class, GVWR, doors, seats
- `engine` (object): Displacement, cylinders, fuel type, horsepower, configuration
- `transmission` (object): Type, speeds
- `dimensions` (object): Curb weight, wheelbase
- `plant` (object): Assembly plant city, state, country
- `safety_equipment` (object): Airbags, ABS, ESC, TPMS, backup camera, etc.
- `recalls` (object): Count and array of recall records (campaign number, component, summary, consequence, remedy)
- `complaints` (object): Count, array of complaints, summary with crash/fire/injury/death counts
- `safety_ratings` (object): NCAP star ratings — overall, frontal driver/passenger, side driver/passenger, rollover
- `fuel_economy` (object): City/highway/combined MPG, annual fuel cost, CO2 tailpipe g/mi, EV range, charge time
- `photos` (object): URLs for front, rear, side, interior, and detail vehicle photos
- `raw_nhtsa` (object): Full 140+ field NHTSA decode

Rate limit: 30 requests/minute per IP

Example:
```
curl https://mcp.vin/api/vin/1HGCM82633A004352
```

### GET /api/vin/:vin/validate — Quick Validation

Local-only validation (no external API calls). Checks checksum, format, WMI decode, and model year.

Parameters:
- `vin` (path, required): VIN to validate

Response fields:
- `valid` (boolean): Whether checksum and format are correct
- `vin` (string): Normalized VIN
- `check_digit` (object): Expected vs actual check digit
- `wmi` (object): Country, region, manufacturer from positions 1-3
- `model_year` (object): Decoded model year from position 10
- `errors` (array): List of validation errors (empty if valid)

Rate limit: 60 requests/minute per IP

### GET /api/vin/:vin/recalls — Recalls Only

Returns NHTSA recall data for the decoded vehicle.

Parameters:
- `vin` (path, required): 17-character VIN

Response: Array of recall objects with campaign_number, component, summary, consequence, remedy, report_date

Rate limit: 30 requests/minute per IP

### GET /api/vin/:vin/complaints — Complaints Only

Returns NHTSA consumer complaints for the decoded vehicle.

Parameters:
- `vin` (path, required): 17-character VIN

Response: Count, complaints array, summary object with crash/fire/injury/death totals

Rate limit: 30 requests/minute per IP

### GET /api/vin/:vin/safety — Safety Ratings Only

Returns NHTSA NCAP 5-star safety ratings for the decoded vehicle.

Parameters:
- `vin` (path, required): 17-character VIN

Response: Rated boolean, overall/frontal/side/rollover star ratings (1-5), complaint and investigation counts

Rate limit: 30 requests/minute per IP

### GET /api/vin/:vin/fuel — Fuel Economy Only

Returns EPA fuel economy data for the decoded vehicle.

Parameters:
- `vin` (path, required): 17-character VIN

Response: City/highway/combined MPG, annual fuel cost, CO2 g/mi, fuel type, EV range (if applicable)

Rate limit: 30 requests/minute per IP

### GET /api/vin/:vin/photo — Vehicle Photo

Redirects (302) to the front-angle stock photo URL for the decoded vehicle.

Parameters:
- `vin` (path, required): 17-character VIN

Rate limit: 60 requests/minute per IP

### POST /api/batch — Batch Decode

Decode up to 50 VINs in a single request via NHTSA batch API.

Body (JSON):
- `vins` (array of strings, required): Array of VINs to decode (max 50)

Response: Array of decode results

Rate limit: 5 requests/minute per IP

### Direct VIN URLs

Visit `https://mcp.vin/{VIN}` (e.g., `https://mcp.vin/1HGCM82633A004352`) to see an interactive web report for any VIN.

## MCP Server

mcp.vin is available as an MCP (Model Context Protocol) server for AI assistants like Claude.

### Connection Methods

Stdio (local, for Claude Code):
```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "vin": {
      "command": "npx",
      "args": ["-y", "vin-mcp"]
    }
  }
}
```

Streamable HTTP (remote, for Claude Desktop / claude.ai):
```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "vin": {
      "url": "https://mcp.vin/mcp"
    }
  }
}
```

Smithery (one command):
```bash
npx -y @smithery/cli install @keptlive/vin-mcp --client claude
```

### MCP Tools

#### decode_vin
Decode a VIN and return a comprehensive vehicle report with specs, recalls, complaints, safety ratings, fuel economy, and photos.

Parameters:
- `vin` (string, required): 17-character Vehicle Identification Number

Returns: Full JSON report with all data sources aggregated

#### validate_vin
Quickly validate a VIN without calling any external APIs. Checks checksum, format, WMI, and model year.

Parameters:
- `vin` (string, required): VIN to validate

Returns: Validation result with check digit, WMI decode, model year, and error list

#### lookup_recalls
Look up recalls for a vehicle. Provide either a VIN or make/model/year combination.

Parameters:
- `vin` (string, optional): VIN to look up recalls for
- `make` (string, optional): Vehicle make (e.g., "Honda")
- `model` (string, optional): Vehicle model (e.g., "Civic")
- `year` (number, optional): Model year (e.g., 2020)

Returns: Array of recall records with campaign details

#### batch_decode
Decode multiple VINs at once using NHTSA batch API.

Parameters:
- `vins` (array of strings, required): Array of VINs to decode (max 50)

Returns: Array of decode results for each VIN

#### list_saved_vins
List VINs saved by a logged-in user.

Parameters:
- `user_token` (string, required): JWT token from website login

Returns: Array of saved VINs with labels, year, make, model

#### save_vin
Save a VIN to a user's collection with an optional label.

Parameters:
- `user_token` (string, required): JWT token from website login
- `vin` (string, required): 17-character VIN to save
- `label` (string, optional): Custom label (e.g., "Dad's truck")

Returns: Confirmation message

#### remove_saved_vin
Remove a VIN from the user's saved collection.

Parameters:
- `user_token` (string, required): JWT token from website login
- `vin` (string, required): VIN to remove

Returns: Confirmation or not-found message

#### get_output_preferences
Get the user's VIN report output preferences (which sections to show/hide).

Parameters:
- `user_token` (string, required): JWT token

Returns: Preference object with boolean flags for each report section

#### update_output_preferences
Update which sections appear in VIN reports.

Parameters:
- `user_token` (string, required): JWT token
- `show_overview` (boolean, optional): Show vehicle overview section
- `show_engine` (boolean, optional): Show engine details
- `show_safety_ratings` (boolean, optional): Show NCAP safety ratings
- `show_fuel_economy` (boolean, optional): Show EPA fuel economy
- `show_recalls` (boolean, optional): Show recall notices
- `show_complaints` (boolean, optional): Show consumer complaints
- `show_safety_equipment` (boolean, optional): Show safety equipment list
- `show_photos` (boolean, optional): Show vehicle photos
- `show_raw_nhtsa` (boolean, optional): Show raw NHTSA decode data

Returns: Confirmation message

## How VINs Work

A VIN (Vehicle Identification Number) is a 17-character code assigned to every vehicle manufactured since 1981:

- Positions 1-3 (WMI): World Manufacturer Identifier — country, region, manufacturer
- Positions 4-8 (VDS): Vehicle Descriptor Section — model, body style, engine, transmission
- Position 9: Check digit — validates VIN using a weighted algorithm
- Position 10: Model year code (A-Y, 1-9 on a 30-year cycle)
- Position 11: Assembly plant code
- Positions 12-17: Sequential production number

Letters I, O, and Q are never used in VINs (avoid confusion with 1, 0, 9).

## Caching

The server uses in-memory LRU caching with TTL:
- Full VIN decodes: 1 hour
- Recalls: 6 hours
- Safety ratings: 24 hours
- Fuel economy: 24 hours

## Tech Stack

- Runtime: Node.js 18+
- Server: Express 5
- MCP SDK: @modelcontextprotocol/sdk (stdio + Streamable HTTP transports)
- Frontend: Vanilla HTML, CSS, JavaScript
- Database: SQLite (better-sqlite3) for user accounts and saved VINs
- Caching: In-memory LRU with TTL
- External dependencies: Zero API keys — all data sources are free public APIs
